name: AudD
type: Identifier (commercial audio fingerprinting API with a free tier)
maintainer: AudD, LLC (commercial vendor; also publishes an official Chrome extension and open-source SDKs/tools under github.com/AudDMusic)
method: Server-side neural-network-based audio fingerprinting matched against a ~160M-track reference database; enterprise endpoint additionally chunk-scans long audio/video files in 12-second windows to find every song within them
required_input: Raw audio bytes via HTTP URL, multipart file upload, or base64-encoded audio in the 'audio' parameter (standard endpoint, 10MB file-size cap); a special stream-monitoring mode also accepts a live stream/YouTube-stream identifier in the form 'youtube:<video_id>' for continuous monitoring via webhook/long-polling
minimum_clip_length: Standard endpoint analyzes up to ~12 seconds of audio per request; no hard published minimum, but very short clips can trigger a 'file too small to fingerprint' error
classification_or_hitrate: Vendor claims #1 ranking 'among 13 Top Recognition APIs' per a ProgrammableWeb comparison, and internal testing on DJ-mix content where 'the best competitor had on average 6.2% worse accuracy across 7 genres' than AudD. No independent third-party benchmark with a raw accuracy percentage was found. [uncertain]
pitch_speed_cover_robustness: Vendor states the service is 'highly accurate even with background noise, low-quality recordings, and short clips' and can isolate music from speech/noise in vlogs, but no explicit published claim about robustness to nightcore/sped-up/pitch-shifted reuploads, live versions, or covers; standard fingerprinting techniques generally degrade under pitch/tempo shifts. [uncertain]
catalog_language_bias: Vendor states a ~160 million track catalog with no public per-region/genre breakdown (K-pop/J-pop/C-pop, anime/VTuber, indie/unclaimed coverage not disclosed). [uncertain]
evaluation_dataset: Accuracy claims are based on AudD's own internal comparative testing (e.g., DJ-mix genre testing) and third-party review aggregation (ProgrammableWeb), not a standard public benchmark like AudioSet, GTZAN, MUSAN, MagnaTagATune, or MAEB. [uncertain]
confidence_calibration: Public docs do not clearly document a numeric confidence/score field with calibration guidance for the standard recognize response; the enterprise endpoint returns per-match timecodes/offsets useful for filtering, but explicit threshold-tuning guidance was not found. [uncertain]
api_availability: Free tier: 300 free requests on signup, no credit card required. Pay-as-you-go: $5 per 1,000 requests, with volume discounts down to $2 per 1,000 requests at higher tiers (e.g., 100k/month for $450, 200k/month for $800, 500k/month for $1,800). Stream monitoring priced separately (~$45/stream/month against AudD's own database, ~$25/month against a customer-provided catalog). Simple bearer-token (api_token) authentication -- no HMAC signing required.
chrome_extension_usability: Confirmed directly usable from a Chrome extension: AudD publishes and maintains an official production Chrome Web Store extension (github.com/AudDMusic/chrome-extension, Manifest V3, current example version 3.1.4) that captures tab audio client-side via the 'tabCapture' permission and calls https://api.audd.io/ directly, declared in host_permissions -- no backend proxy required for the core recognition call. The identify endpoint itself was directly verified to return 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *'.
audio_access_requirement: Requires raw audio; in the official extension this is obtained via chrome.tabCapture (which requires user-invoked activation, e.g., clicking the extension's action icon) or by supplying a media URL. It would fail to capture audio from DRM-protected playback paths and cannot recognize muted/blocked tabs; age-restricted YouTube videos should still work as long as tab audio is actually playing.
client_vs_server: Because the API token can be used directly from the client (no secret-signing scheme), audio (or a URL/identifier referencing it) can be sent straight from the user's browser to AudD's servers, without a mandatory first-party backend intermediary -- simpler privacy story but also means the API token is exposed in the shipped extension code, enabling potential token abuse/quota theft unless mitigated (e.g., per-user tokens, rate-limiting, or a lightweight proxy).
bundle_weight_cold_start: No ML model ships inside the extension; recognition is entirely server-side, so bundle weight is minimal (just the extension's own JS/UI code). Vendor states standard-endpoint response time is 'under 2 seconds', implying low cold-start overhead beyond the network round-trip of uploading a short audio clip.
breakage_risk: Official, actively maintained commercial API with an actual shipping Chrome extension as a reference implementation (regularly updated, e.g., manifest v3 migration already done) -- low technical breakage risk compared to unofficial/reverse-engineered surfaces; primary risk is pricing/quota changes rather than the API disappearing.
realtime_capability: Vendor-stated standard-endpoint response time of 'under 2 seconds' makes it feasible for in-browser, near-instant recognition once a short audio sample has been captured and uploaded.
identification_fields: Standard response includes artist, title, album, release_date, label, timecode, and song_link by default; optional 'return' parameter adds Apple Music, Spotify, Deezer, MusicBrainz metadata, and lyrics. ISRC and UPC are documented as returned fields, reported as gated to Startup-plan-and-above accounts per one comparison source. [uncertain] on exact minimum plan tier required for ISRC.
isrc_availability: Yes -- ISRC and UPC are returned as part of the metadata response (reported as available starting from the Startup paid plan tier rather than the free tier). [uncertain] whether the free tier includes ISRC.
karaoke_specific_outputs: No BPM, musical key, vocal/instrumental separation, or word-level lyric timing in the core recognition response; the optional lyrics return field provides full lyrics text (not necessarily time-synced/word-level) via a third-party lyrics provider. No confirmed karaoke-grade timing output. [uncertain]
tos_restrictions: Commercial ToS govern reselling/redistributing raw recognition results and set per-plan usage limits; AudD's own official tooling (e.g., the youtube-recognizer sample project and the Chrome extension) directly interacts with YouTube tab audio/streams, which is a first-party-sanctioned integration pattern rather than a scraping violation, but the exact current AudD Terms of Service text should be reviewed directly for redistribution/caching restrictions. [uncertain] on precise current clause wording.
risk_tolerance_note: Because AudD is an official, contractually-licensed commercial vendor with its own production Chrome extension as precedent, it carries materially lower ToS/legal risk than reverse-engineered options like SongRec; residual risk is around exposing the API token client-side leading to quota abuse rather than legal exposure to the developer.
cascade_position: Well suited as either a cheap-ish enrichment step or even a primary identification call given its low per-request cost ($5/1,000 = $0.005/request) and sub-2-second latency; still likely gated behind a lightweight music-vs-non-music classifier to avoid spending paid quota identifying non-music content.
failure_mode: Fails relatively silently with an empty/no-match result rather than confidently hallucinating, since it is fingerprint-based matching against a real catalog rather than generative guessing -- lowers risk of a visibly wrong karaoke overlay, though close-variant tracks (same song, different official remix) could still produce a technically-correct-but-not-exact match.
cost_model_at_scale: At $5 per 1,000 requests (or as low as $2/1,000 at high volume), a free consumer extension issuing even one identification call per user session could scale into real recurring cost quickly beyond the 300 free trial requests; e.g., 10,000 sessions/month at 1 call each would cost roughly $50/month at standard pricing, and dedicated stream-monitoring is priced per-stream/month rather than per-call.
geo_region_availability: No public evidence of hard geo-blocking of the API itself; the underlying 160M-track catalog's regional/label licensing completeness is not broken out by market. [uncertain]
